AR-2026F-SR6.aiSummary: This resolution would let a bill be introduced to create the Equal Distribution County Turnback Fund and give counties extra money from certain state tax revenue. Each fiscal year, once the fund reaches $150 million, the state would send $2 million to each county, with most of that money for roads, water and sewer work, and county equipment. The rest would support fire, law enforcement, or other county community projects. It also says the act would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SR37.aiSummary: This resolution would bar Arkansas Girls State from using the Senate chamber for its 2026 meeting and would also block access to the Bureau of Legislative Research’s bill drafting help during that meeting. It would be lifted if the Senate’s president pro tempore finds that the American Legion Auxiliary has let certain students, who were denied because of missed deadlines, take part in the 2026 meeting. The resolution also urges the American Legion Auxiliary to rethink any decision that would keep those students from participating.

AR-2026F-HB1035.aiSummary: The bill would fund the Arkansas Department of Health’s tobacco prevention and cessation programs for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets staff limits, including 31 regular employees and up to 4 temporary workers, and gives the program $14,702,255. It also lets the department move $500,000 from the prevention and cessation account to the Breast Cancer Control Fund for the state match on breast and cervical cancer services. The emergency clause was adopted, and the act would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1017.aiSummary: This act sets spending for the Arkansas Department of Agriculture’s promotion boards for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. It gives money for the beef, catfish, corn and grain sorghum, rice, soybean, and wheat boards, with set amounts for operations, research, and related work. It also lets the state fiscal officer waive some fund deductions for certain agriculture fees from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the act takes effect on July 1, 2026.
